Polsky 10: Pyxis secures up to $282.6M | Thrixel launches with new $3M | Inomagen receives $2.9M grant
October 12, 2026
The Polsky 10 is a bi-weekly newsletter featuring 10 things to know from the University of Chicago’s Polsky Center. To get the Polsky 10 sent directly to your inbox every other Friday, sign up here >>
1 // Pyxis Oncology announces up to $282.6M in new funding as it gears up for key clinical milestones.
UChicago Startup Investment Program recipient Pyxis Oncology has raised approximately $110M in a recent public offering to advance its lead cancer therapy, micvotabart pelidotin (MICVO), toward key clinical milestones. The Boston-based biotech, founded on the research from UChicago Professor Thomas Gajewski, AB ’84, PhD ’89, MD ’91, could raise up to another $172.6M based on milestone-linked warrants following the company’s expected release of overall survival data in the first half of 2027. This latest financing gives Pyxis the resources to move MICVO into its next stage of development, including a planned Phase 3 trial in recurrent and metastatic head and neck cancer, as it works to determine whether the antibody-drug conjugate can deliver on promising early clinical results. Read more now .
2 // Thrixel just launched with $3M in funding to take AI to another dimension.
As AI continues to revolutionize the way we produce images, text, graphics, and code, there has been one lasting creativity barrier that AI has struggled to climb… 3D content. The complicated design and building process demands deep technical expertise, beyond the scope of most developers. But now, UChicago computer scientist Rana Hanocka is turning her years of research in AI and computer graphics into a new company to end this roadblock. Thrixel is a 3D creation platform designed to make it easier for AI agents to generate, manipulate, and animate 3D objects. To assist development in the AI pipeline, Thrixel creates structured assets whose individual parts — like a car’s wheels, doors, and chassis — can be identified and manipulated independently, making them easier to use in games, robotics, simulations, and other interactive applications. Alongside news of its launch, Thrixel also announced a raise of $3M in inception funding. Read more now .
3 // This UChicago faculty-founded biotech is getting to the heart of AFib with a new $2.9M grant.
Inomagen Therapeutics , founded by UChicago cardiologist Rishi Arora, is developing a non-viral gene therapy to improve the treatment of atrial fibrillation (AF). Specifically, Inomagen’s goal is to create a more durable, disease-modifying alternative to current AF treatments that aren’t effective enough for many patients. Most recently, the biotech has been awarded an NIH Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) grant providing up to $2.9M to advance its investigational gene therapy. The two-year award will support preclinical safety and efficacy studies, as well as manufacturing work needed to prepare the therapy for a future Investigational New Drug application with the FDA. Furthermore, this grant builds on $3.67M in previous NIH SBIR funding for Inomagen’s AF program. Read more now .

articles.title: The RMR Group Secures $272.1 Million Refinancing For Cedars-Sinai Medical Office Portfolio In Los Angeles
articles.snippet:
The RMR Group announced that it facilitated a $272.1 million interest-only mortgage financing on behalf of a managed joint venture for a medical office portfolio located on the Cedars-Sinai Medical Center campus in Los Angeles.
The post The RMR Group Secures $272.1 Million Refinancing For Cedars-Sinai Medical Office Portfolio In Los Angeles appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
The RMR Group Secures $272.1 Million Refinancing For Cedars-Sinai Medical Office Portfolio In Los Angeles
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 12, 2026
The RMR Group Secures $272.1 Million Refinancing For Cedars-Sinai Medical Office Portfolio In Los Angeles
The RMR Group announced that it facilitated a $272.1 million interest-only mortgage financing on behalf of a managed joint venture for a medical office portfolio located on the Cedars-Sinai Medical Center campus in Los Angeles.
The financing is secured by 8631 and 8635 West Third Street, two 11-story medical office buildings totaling approximately 330,000 square feet, along with two structured parking garages.
The buildings are connected to Cedars-Sinai Medical Center by skybridge.
Cedars-Sinai and its affiliates serve as the portfolio’s anchor tenants and occupy approximately 60% of the total rentable square footage.
The new loan has an initial two-year term with three one-year extension options.
It carries an interest rate of one-month Term SOFR plus 180 basis points.
Proceeds were used to repay approximately $267 million of existing mortgage debt that was scheduled to mature in February 2027 and to cover closing costs.
The refinancing provides the joint venture with additional term flexibility while maintaining financing for a strategically located healthcare real estate asset.
Morgan Stanley and BNP Paribas provided the financing.
Hogan Lovells Cadwalader US LLP served as counsel to the lenders, while Sullivan & Worcester LLP represented the borrower.
The portfolio is owned by a joint venture for which RMR provides asset and property management services.
The venture is primarily owned by private institutional investors.
Diversified Healthcare Trust, an RMR client, owns a 20% equity interest in the joint venture.
RMR manages more than $37 billion in assets under management through a platform supported by more than 800 real estate professionals across more than 30 offices nationwide.
The firm focuses on commercial real estate, residential real estate, and related businesses.
KEY QUOTES:
“This refinancing reflects the quality of this medical office portfolio, which is located on the campus of one of the nation’s leading healthcare institutions. By refinancing its upcoming maturity with a new loan that provides term extension flexibility, the joint venture is well positioned to continue benefiting from the portfolio’s strong anchor tenancy, strategic location and attractive long-term fundamentals. The successful execution of this transaction underscores the value of RMR’s integrated real estate platform and our ability to deliver capital solutions that support our clients’ investment objectives.”
Adam Portnoy, President and Chief Executive Officer of The RMR Group

articles.snippet:
SMT Energy has formed an equity partnership with Climate Adaptive Infrastructure for up to $268 million at the parent-company level to accelerate the development, construction and operation of battery energy storage projects across the U.S.
The post SMT Energy Secures Up To $268 Million Equity Partnership With Climate Adaptive Infrastructure appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
SMT Energy Secures Up To $268 Million Equity Partnership With Climate Adaptive Infrastructure
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 2, 2026
SMT Energy Secures Up To $268 Million Equity Partnership With Climate Adaptive Infrastructure
SMT Energy has formed an equity partnership with Climate Adaptive Infrastructure for up to $268 million at the parent-company level to accelerate the development, construction and operation of battery energy storage projects across the U.S.
The new commitment is in addition to $32 million previously deployed by CAI into SMT assets. Combined with project-level debt, tax equity and other capital sources, SMT expects the investment to support energy infrastructure with an aggregate value significantly greater than CAI’s equity commitment.
SMT develops, owns and operates battery energy storage systems. Its portfolio includes distributed-generation battery projects, utility-scale storage projects and powered-land developments designed to support grid reliability and rising electricity demand.
The partnership is intended to provide long-term capital for projects across multiple U.S. markets as battery storage takes a larger role in supporting renewable generation and balancing the electric grid.
SMT said the capital will allow the company to accelerate its existing project-development pipeline and pursue additional infrastructure opportunities.
Expedition Infrastructure Partners served as financial adviser to SMT Energy. Stoel Rives served as legal counsel to SMT, while Orrick served as legal counsel to CAI.
KEY QUOTES:
“This partnership is a defining milestone for SMT Energy. CAI gives us the capital and support needed to move faster and build at greater scale. We are grateful to Bill Green and the entire CAI team for their confidence in our platform and our people.”
JJ Switzer, Co-Founder and Co-CEO of SMT Energy
“CAI is relentlessly focused on the macro trends driving the future of global infrastructure, and this investment in SMT fits squarely into a key CAI inevitability: as wind and solar proliferate as the most efficient and fastest ways to deploy new power, battery energy storage is increasingly critical for grid stabilization. We are proud to back a team with such an impressive track record as they scale into the next phase of growth.”
Bill Green, Managing Partner of Climate Adaptive Infrastructure

articles.title: Ironbark Financial Group Secures $255.9 Million Investment From Merchant Wealth Partners
articles.snippet:
Ironbark Financial Group secured a $255.9 million investment from Merchant Wealth Partners to support the next stage of the Australian financial services firm's growth.
The post Ironbark Financial Group Secures $255.9 Million Investment From Merchant Wealth Partners appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Ironbark Financial Group Secures $255.9 Million Investment From Merchant Wealth Partners
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 12, 2026
Ironbark Financial Group Secures $255.9 Million Investment From Merchant Wealth Partners
Ironbark Financial Group secured a $255.9 million investment from Merchant Wealth Partners to support the next stage of the Australian financial services firm’s growth.
The transaction represents Merchant Wealth Partners’ largest investment outside the U.S.
Merchant will join existing Ironbark investors including Soul Patts, management, employees, and other shareholders.
The new capital is intended to accelerate Ironbark’s growth strategy in Australia and support future expansion.
Ironbark expects the partnership to provide additional capabilities across wealth management, artificial intelligence, technology, and operations.
Founded in 2009, Ironbark has more than $97 billion in funds under advice, management, and trusteeship as of June 30, 2026.
Its operations span three primary businesses: Ironbark Advice, Ironbark Private Wealth, and Ironbark Investment Solutions.
Merchant Wealth Partners provides strategic growth capital and support to independent financial services businesses, particularly wealth and asset management firms.
Merchant’s broader network includes more than 125 partner firms and financial services practices across six countries with more than $300 billion in combined assets under management.
Soul Patts will remain an investor and continue working alongside Ironbark and Merchant as the company pursues its growth strategy.
The investment follows several leadership appointments at Ironbark.
Chris Larsen serves as Managing Director and Executive Chair, while Justin Greiner was appointed Group CEO.
Founding partners Brendan Carpenter, Alex Donald, and David Stephen continue in senior leadership roles.
Ironbark said the capital will also provide liquidity for shareholders and support a pipeline of potential strategic acquisitions.
The transaction remains subject to customary regulatory approvals, including review by Australia’s Foreign Investment Review Board and the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission.
KEY QUOTES:
“Merchant’s credentials as a long-term, patient investor with global expertise make it an ideal partner for Ironbark. Importantly, we have a strong cultural and strategic alignment, underpinned by a shared long-term outlook, partnership mindset and commitment to supporting founder-led businesses.”
Chris Larsen, Managing Director and Executive Chair of Ironbark Financial Group
“We partner with exceptional businesses and management teams where we believe our capital, capabilities and global network can help support their long-term ambitions. Ironbark has built a differentiated financial services platform of significant scale, with an outstanding leadership team and a clear vision for the future.”
Marc Spilker, Executive Chairman of Merchant Wealth Partners
“For close to a decade Soul Patts has supported Ironbark’s evolution, and we welcome Merchant joining the business. Merchant’s ecosystem gives Ironbark access to deeper expertise that will broaden its client offering.”
David Scammell, Managing Director, Principal Investments at Soul Patts

articles.title: Three Corners Connector Selected For Negotiations On Up To $250 Million DOE SPARK Award
articles.snippet:
Three Corners Connector has been selected to proceed to negotiations for potential funding of up to $250 million through the U.S. Department of Energy's Speed to Power through Accelerated Reconductoring and other Key Advanced Transmission Technology Upgrades, or SPARK, program.
The post Three Corners Connector Selected For Negotiations On Up To $250 Million DOE SPARK Award appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Three Corners Connector Selected For Negotiations On Up To $250 Million DOE SPARK Award
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 7, 2026
Three Corners Connector Selected For Negotiations On Up To $250 Million DOE SPARK Award
Three Corners Connector has been selected to proceed to negotiations for potential funding of up to $250 million through the U.S. Department of Energy’s Speed to Power through Accelerated Reconductoring and other Key Advanced Transmission Technology Upgrades, or SPARK, program.
The Oklahoma Office of Management and Enterprise Services applied for the federal funding with Three Corners Connector serving as a subrecipient.
Selection for negotiations does not represent a final award. Funding remains subject to successful negotiations and execution of a formal financial assistance agreement.
Three Corners Connector is a proposed 300-mile high-voltage direct current interregional transmission line connecting the eastern and western electric grids, with endpoints in Oklahoma and Colorado.
The project is designed to more than double the existing 1,320 MW transfer capacity between the two grids.
If finalized, SPARK funding would primarily support engineering and materials associated with the project’s transmission towers.
The project is intended to improve interregional grid connectivity and provide utilities and grid operators with increased ability to move electricity between the Southwest Power Pool and Western Electricity Coordinating Council markets.
Three Corners Connector is progressing through regulatory filings, with final approvals expected in 2026.
Construction is expected to begin after remaining land rights are secured and required regulatory approvals are obtained. The project could become operational as early as 2031.
KEY QUOTES:
“It’s not that we don’t have enough electricity in most areas. Most of the time we lack the transmission capabilities to go from one region where it’s being generated to another region where it’s needed. So the connectors that we’re investing in across the U.S. are ensuring that we have capacity to move the power and energy to where it’s needed.”
Kyle Haustveit, U.S. Department of Energy Under Secretary of Energy
“The Great Plains is a cornerstone of the country’s energy system, and connecting the eastern and western grids here strengthens reliability on both sides. Selection for SPARK funding helps Oklahoma and Three Corners Connector build toward a more resilient energy future, and we look forward to advancing the project alongside the stakeholders who have helped shape its development.”
Bryant Coon, Senior Director of Development for Three Corners Connector
